input.question: Why does a slightly hot shower feel like you are burning when it touches your skin, while a hot tub set at 102F feels comfortable when you get into it?
input.ground_truth: In addition, a hot tub has its water somewhat static. When you enter, the hot water transfers its heat to you but stays roughly where it is, so it kind of forms a shield of slightly colder water around you. You notice, when you move inside the tub it gets hotter briefly. In a shower, there's new hot water constantly touching your body, its gonna be hotter.

Question: Why does a slightly hot shower feel like you are burning when it touches your skin, while a hot tub set at 102F feels comfortable when you get into it?

That’s because it’s a lot of water in one spot, all at once. That’s like the hot shower—it’s hot water coming at your skin all at once, so it feels like it’s burning.

But if you jump into a big pool or a hot tub that’s warm all around you, your whole body gets warm at the same time. Your skin gets used to it, little by little, so it doesn’t feel like it’s burning. It feels cozy, like a big warm hug!
